\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غار} (ghâr)}{غار (ghâr)}]{\fa{غار} (ghâr) — a cave}

\label{lesson:FA-C468-ghar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for grass, then the Persian for to prune.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غار}}
\textbf{\fa{غار}} (\emph{ghâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{کوه} \fa{یک} \fa{غار} \fa{تاریک} \fa{پیدا} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar kuh yek ghâr-e târik peydâ kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We found a dark cave in the mountains.
\end{quote}

Note the letter \fa{غ}, said \emph{gh}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ghâr} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ġār} 'grotto, cave' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ghâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for grass, then the Persian for to prune, then say \emph{ghâr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دامنه} (dâmane)}{دامنه (dâmane)}]{\fa{دامنه} (dâmane) — a slope, a mountainside; a range (of a thing)}

\label{lesson:FA-C468-damane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to prune, then the Persian for a cave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دامنه}}
\textbf{\fa{دامنه}} (\emph{dâmane}) — \textquotedblleft{}a slope, a mountainside; a range (of a thing)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روستا} \fa{در} \fa{دامنه} \fa{کوه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rustâ dar dâmane-ye kuh ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The village is on the mountainside.
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{dâman} 'skirt, hem': the skirt of the mountain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dâmane} is built on native \emph{dâman} 'skirt, hem', with the ending \emph{-e}: the hem of a mountain. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گردنه} (gardane)}{گردنه (gardane)}]{\fa{گردنه} (gardane) — a mountain pass}

\label{lesson:FA-C468-gardane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cave, then the Persian for a slope.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گردنه}}
\textbf{\fa{گردنه}} (\emph{gardane}) — \textquotedblleft{}a mountain pass\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{زمستان} \fa{گردنه} \fa{پر} \fa{از} \fa{برف} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar zemestân gardane por az barf ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In winter the pass is full of snow.
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{gardan} 'neck': the neck between two peaks.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gardane} is a native word, which EtymDB lists; it is built on \emph{gardan} 'neck', the narrow neck of land between two heights.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کوهپایه} (kuhpâye)}{کوهپایه (kuhpâye)}]{\fa{کوهپایه} (kuhpâye) — the foothills}

\label{lesson:FA-C468-kuhpaye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a slope, then the Persian for a mountain pass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کوهپایه}}
\textbf{\fa{کوهپایه}} (\emph{kuhpâye}) — \textquotedblleft{}the foothills\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شهر} \fa{ما} \fa{در} \fa{کوهپایه} \fa{است} \fa{و} \fa{هوایش} \fa{خنک} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shahr-e mâ dar kuhpâye ast va havâyash khonak ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our town is in the foothills and its air is cool.
\end{quote}

\emph{kuh} 'mountain' + \emph{pâye} 'base, foot'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kuhpâye} is a native compound of \emph{kuh} 'mountain', from Middle Persian \emph{kōf} (EtymDB), and \emph{pâye} 'foot, base', from \emph{pâ} 'foot'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صعود} \fa{کردن} (so'ud kardan)}{صعود کردن (so'ud kardan)}]{\fa{صعود} \fa{کردن} (so'ud kardan) — to climb, to ascend (a mountain)}

\label{lesson:FA-C468-soud-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a mountain pass, then the Persian for the foothills.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صعود} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{صعود} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{so'ud kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to climb, to ascend (a mountain)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کوهنوردها} \fa{صبح} \fa{زود} \fa{به} \fa{قله} \fa{صعود} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kuhnavard-hâ sobh-e zud be qolle so'ud kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The climbers climbed to the summit early in the morning.
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{bâlâ raftan}; the top takes \emph{be}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{so'ud kardan} is built from \emph{so'ud} 'ascent', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{ṣuʿūd}, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a mountain pass, then the Persian for the foothills, then say \emph{so'ud kardan} again
